result.rationale: Verified in the diff: the delete() action calls this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', ...) }) with no .catch, while save() in the same component uses .catch(popupAjaxError). A rejected DELETE promise therefore resolves nowhere: no error popup, no state change, and the row silently remains — the exact asymmetric behavior the finding describes. The mechanism is fully visible in the diff; whether maintainers deem it a shipping bug vs. a polish item is the only uncertainty.

judged_text: delete() attaches only a .then to destroyRecord() with no .catch, so a failed DELETE (server error, session expiry, network drop) is swallowed as an unhandled rejection while save() on the same component routes failures to popupAjaxError. The admin clicks delete, confirms, and the row silently stays in the table with no error popup and no state change; the failure is invisible unless they happen to reload the page and see the host still present.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` without a `.catch(...)`, unlike `save()` which uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. If the DELETE fails, the promise rejection is not handled here and no error UI is triggered, so the admin gets no feedback and the row will remain (since `deleteHost` is only sent in the `then`).
